### Added
- **`Awaiting Session`: a per-session server's state says whether it works.** An MCPServer whose callers bring their own identity (`auth.forwardToken`, `auth.tokenExchange`) holds no connection of its own and, with no session connected, read `Auth Required` -- the same state as a server waiting for a person to sign in through muster, and the same state whether every exchange succeeded or none could. Such a server now reads `Awaiting Session` (service state `awaiting_session`, Normal event `MCPServerAwaitingSession`) wherever it read `Auth Required` before: after the probe, after the last session's connection is lost, after an automatic recovery reached it; `Auth Required` keeps its one meaning. A `tokenExchange` server verifies its client credentials Secret at start and is `Failed` with the Secret named while it is missing, retried with the reconnect backoff so a Secret that arrives later heals it. Every per-user exchange the aggregator performs reaches the server's state: a failure every caller shares (the credentials Secret, `invalid_client`, a token endpoint that does not answer or answers 5xx, an unknown connector) puts the server in `Failed` with the exchange error as `lastError`, and the next successful exchange, a restart or a spec change returns it to `Awaiting Session`; a failure of the caller's own token stays that session's. The reconciler writes a `Ready` condition for every server whose reason names the state (`AwaitingSession`, `Connected`, `AuthRequired`, `Suspended`, ...) or the class of an exchange failure (`TokenExchangeCredentials`, `TokenExchangeEndpoint`, `TokenExchangeConnector`) and whose message explains it -- for `Awaiting Session` the mechanism, the token endpoint and connector, and when the last exchange succeeded. `muster list mcpserver`, `core_service_status`, the CRDs of both charts and the reference docs carry the state; `core_service_start` and `core_service_restart` on such a server say what it waits for instead of pointing at a sign-in that does not exist. The scenario `oauth-sso-token-exchange-state` pins the states through a real RFC 8693 exchange against the harness's authorization server. ([#1300](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1300))
